note: Codified from the City of Belton Zoning Ordinance No. 22790-1 (originally adopted 1990-02-20, repealing prior Ordinance 12975-1 of 1975-12-09), text current through Ordinance 2025-47 (adopted 2025-07-22), PDF republished by the City on 2026-08-11 as "Zoning Ordinance with Cover and Appendix Updated 8-11-26.pdf" -- the current, live document at the cited URL as of 2026-09-06. This is a classic enumerated Euclidean ordinance (Sections 8-31 define one base district each with its own numbered AREA REGULATIONS subsection), NOT a form-based code, so front/side/rear/corner numbers are direct district-specific citations rather than build-to-line ranges. DISAMBIGUATION: belton.org and the domain-adjacent "City of Belton" planning pages surfaced by generic web search are Belton, MISSOURI (Cass County, MO; Municode client library.municode.com/mo/belton) -- a same-name, different-state city. This table is sourced exclusively from beltontexas.gov / Bell County TX primary documents; no Missouri content was used. Belton, TX's Code of Ordinances is split across two properties: Municode (library.municode.com/tx/belton, a JavaScript-shell SPA that returns no server-rendered ordinance text to a non-browser fetch -- confirmed empty on direct fetch) and an eLaws.us mirror (belton-tx.elaws.us/code/coor_ch17), which DOES render but covers only Chapter 17 Article II (the Planning and Zoning Commission's establishment, Sec. 17-16 through 17-19) -- the substantive Zoning Ordinance with its district-by-district dimensional standards is NOT codified into either the Municode or eLaws copies of the base Code of Ordinances; it is maintained by the City as its own standalone document, linked from the beltontexas.gov Planning Department page and hosted on the City's Revize CMS at the citation_url above. There is no separate Municode "unified_development_code" product for Belton, TX (unlike Belton, MO, which does have one at the analogous URL -- verified this does NOT exist for the TX city via search, not assumed from an HTTP 200 on the SPA route, which returns 200 for any client-routed path regardless of whether the underlying product exists). GIS zoning codes verified live against the City's own ArcGIS FeatureServer (services5.arcgis.com/FkDUU6xkZJTbBa9X/arcgis/rest/services/Planning/FeatureServer/6, field Zoning_Abbr, queried 2026-09-06) match every base-district code coded here (A, RE, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, PH, 2F, MF, MH, O-1, O-2, UC-1, UC-2, NS, R, CH, C-1, C-2, LI, HI, RD) except IP (Industrial Park, Section 26), which is defined in the ordinance but did not appear in the live GIS distinct-value sample -- included anyway since the ordinance text is real and a future parcel could carry it. OMITTED: CD/CBD (Section 22's own text says "This section has been replaced by the adopted Imagine Belton Standards" -- a separate, not-yet-located form-based-code document, analogous to how the existing Taylor and Hutto tables exclude their form-based/transect chapters); the live GIS layer also carries codes MS ("Main Street"), U ("Uptown"), T ("Transition"), and N ("Neighborhood") that do not appear anywhere in this Zoning Ordinance's district list (Sections 8-31) and are inferred -- NOT confirmed -- to be transect/place-type zones defined in that same replaced-by-Imagine-Belton-Standards document; no numeric standards are asserted for CD, MS, U, T, or N here. Also omitted: HP Historic Preservation Overlay (Section 29), CR Residential Conservation and Revitalization Overlay (Section 30), and PD Planned Development (Section 32) -- these are overlay/prefix districts layered on a base zoning district rather than independent dimensional standards, and the live GIS data shows the overwhelming majority of Belton's actual PD-prefixed parcels carry unique per-ordinance conditions (e.g. "PD-C1 Wedding Chapel", "PD-SF-1-SUP") that cannot be reduced to one table row without reading each individual PD ordinance, which was out of scope for this pass. SUP (Specific Use Permit, Section 33) is a permit overlay, not a district, and is likewise omitted. Sign regulations (Section 38) are bound into the same PDF as "Section 38" per the Planning Department page's own description ("Includes Sign Ordinance as Section 38") but are a distinct regulatory subject and are not reflected in this setback table. MODELING NOTES ACROSS ALL 22 CODIFIED DISTRICTS: (1) Height is stated in STORIES rather than feet for A, RE, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, PH, 2F, MF, C-1, C-2, and RD; max_height_ft is a non-binding 100 sentinel for all of these, matching the established repo convention (see taylor-tx.json, hutto-tx.json) of never converting a stories-only standard into a fabricated feet number. MH (Section 16) has NO height regulations subsection at all -- height is entirely unaddressed for that district. CH, IP, O-2, and UC-1 state height as unlimited ("None") with no stories figure either; UC-2 uses an unlimited-height-with-scaling-setback formula. Only NS (20 ft), R (40 ft), LI (35 ft), and HI (60 ft) state a true numeric height maximum in feet, and those four are coded as real, human-verified values. (2) No district in this ordinance defines a separate "impervious cover" percentage anywhere -- confirmed by a full-text search of the entire 10,134-line extracted document for the string "impervious", which returns zero hits used as a zoning standard; max_impervious_pct is a not_specified 100 sentinel for all 22 districts. Only "lot coverage" (building footprint) is regulated, and only for some districts. (3) Where the ordinance states a base value plus a conditional exception (e.g. O-1's rear yard being 0 generally but 10 ft when adjoining a residential district; HI's side/rear yard being 0 generally but 60 ft near residential districts or where wall openings face the line), the GENERAL/BASE case is codified as the district's number and the conditional exception is preserved verbatim in that field's provenance quote, matching the precedent set by hutto-tx.json's treatment of its B-1/B-2 residential-adjacency exceptions. (4) PH (Patio Home, Section 13) is a genuine zero-lot-line district with an asymmetric 8-inch/10-foot side yard rather than a single flat side setback; side_ft is coded 0 with not_specified:true and a quote carrying the full real standard -- treat this as flagged-for-review rather than a clean number. (5) O-2's (Section 18) side-yard clause is internally ambiguous in the source PDF between a "None (interior)" reading and a "twenty-five feet (25') adjacent side property lines" reading that appear in the same sentence without a clear delimiter; side_ft is coded 0 (interior/base) at reduced confidence (0.55, asserted) and the ambiguity is called out explicitly rather than silently resolved -- this is the single lowest-confidence numeric value in the table and should be confirmed against the ordinance before being treated as final. (6) Two apparent drafting typos in the source ordinance are preserved verbatim in citation quotes rather than silently corrected: C-2's lot-coverage subsection reads "Fifty permit (50%)" (Section 25.4.C) and IP's lot-coverage subsection is labeled "Minimum Lot Coverage" (Section 26.4.C) where every other district uses "Maximum Lot Coverage" -- both are coded at the evident intended value (50% and not_specified respectively) with the typo flagged.

[sic -- ordinance text says "rear setback" in the side-yard clause, an apparent drafting cross-reference error; 0 is the general-case base, 60 ft is a real conditional exception near residential districts or where wall openings face the property line.]

side_corner_ft.quote: Section 28.4 states no separate corner-lot / street-side-adjacent side yard for this district; mirrors the base side yard (0, subject to the same 60 ft residential/openings exception).

max_height_ft.quote: 28.3 HEIGHT REGULATIONS: Maximum Height - Sixty feet (60') or three (3) stories.

max_lot_coverage_pct.quote: C. Maximum Lot Coverage: In no case shall more than fifty percent (50%) of the lot area be covered by the main building and accessory buildings.

max_impervious_pct.quote: Full-text search of the Belton Zoning Ordinance (all 53 sections plus appendix) finds zero occurrences of "impervious" used as a zoning-cap concept anywhere in the document; only "lot coverage" (building footprint, defined per district in the AREA REGULATIONS subsection) is regulated where stated. No impervious-cover standard exists to cite for this or any district.

side_ft.quote: Minimum Side Yard - Five feet (5'); twenty-five feet (25') adjacent to a street

side_corner_ft.quote: Minimum Side Yard - Five feet (5'); twenty-five feet (25') adjacent to a street

max_height_ft.quote: Maximum Height - two and one-half (2 1/2) stories (Section 31.3). Height is stated in stories, not feet, for this district; 100 is a non-binding sentinel, not an asserted feet entitlement.

max_lot_coverage_pct.quote: C. Maximum Lot Coverage: Forty percent (40%)
